messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired for synthetic check rdw-prober-eu-west-1 — 6 consecutive failures in 2m. probe_id=rdw-prober-eu-west-1, rule=synth-http-availability, group=canary
pagerduty: Incident INC-2026-00123 created and paged oncall schedule 'infra-eu-rotation' — urgency=high
maya: saw this on my phone, jumping in. Grafana shows a spike of 502s from the prober in eu-west-1 starting 1m ago. link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/synth/rdw-prober-eu-west-1 (live)
liam: confirming — probes started failing around 2026-03-15T09:12:00Z. Backend error rate for inference-gateway-eu also ticked up ~0.8% error budget in the same window.
maya: quick check: curl against the canary endpoint returns 502 consistently from two vantage points.
maya: ```
curl -v https://rdw-prober-eu-west-1.redwood-infra/synth-check
> HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
``` 
sophia: I'm oncall, ack'ing in PD and taking this. Starting triage.
oncall-bridge: handoff note: sophia took ownership. previous oncall liam -> sophia. PagerDuty shows ack by sophia.
liam: thx. I can stay on work item for mitigation steps. initial hypothesis: edge proxy (fastly/nginx) returning 502 due to upstream connection failures — recent config change rolled out to edge-eu ~09:10Z?
alex: I see a small config-stage deploy around 09:09Z to the edge fleet (edge-config v2.14.1). Could be related. Rolling back config is an option but want to avoid noisy rollback.
sophia: runbook step 1: check probe fanout settings and whether the prober is amplifying transient auth failures. Runbook link: https://wiki.redwood.ai/runbooks/synthetic
maya: checking prober logs now — looks like the prober is receiving `connection reset by peer` from upstreams rather than auth errors. Dumping last 100 lines.
maya: ```
[09:12:03Z] prober: request -> inference-gateway-eu (10.2.12.45): connect: connection reset
[09:12:04Z] prober: retrying (1/3)
[09:12:05Z] prober: request -> inference-gateway-eu (10.2.12.47): connect: connection reset
``` 
liam: that aligns with a brief networking blip between edge and gateway. Could be a flapping route or capacity saturation on a small subset of gw hosts.
sophia: mitigation options:
- reduce prober fanout to 1 for eu to stop noisy paging
- scale inference-gateway-eu up by +2 replicas in the EU pool
- add temporary routing to eu-failover-region for prober traffic
Which one first?
maya: recommend lowering fanout (non-invasive) while we confirm root cause. Doing quick patch to prober config in eu to set `fanout: 1` and `timeout: 5s`.
liam: I'll prepare a quick K8s patch if needed. sophia, want me to apply the scale-up as well?
sophia: go ahead with patch for fanout. Hold on scale until we see if errors drop.
maya: applying config patch now to prober deployment eu-west-1:
maya: ```bash
kubectl -n infra patch cm rdw-prober-config -p '{"data":{"fanout":"1","timeout":"5s"}}'
kubectl -n infra rollout restart deployment/rdw-prober-eu-west-1
``` 
maya: patched and restarted prober pods — new pods coming up (2/2 ready)
liam: looking at Grafana — failures fell from 6 -> 0 over the last 30s. Good signal.
sophia: nice. paging suppressed, update PD incident with mitigation performed.
pagerduty: Incident INC-2026-00123 — acknowledged by sophia. Status: mitigation in progress. Notes: patched prober fanout -> 1 in eu-west-1.
alex: I'll keep an eye on edge-config rollback risk. No further edge deploys scheduled for next 30m.
maya: also verified customer-facing product metrics: user-facing 5xx count rose ~0.3% but returned to baseline after mitigation. No active customer support tickets tied to this window so far.
sophia: customer impact note: transient elevated 502s in eu region between 09:12-09:14Z. Estimated request failure rate ~0.3% of EU traffic. Not SLA impacting but should be in the postmortem.
liam: root-cause investigation next: check for noisy kernel logs on the gateway hosts (possible conntrack exhaustion) and review recent edge-config change diff.
maya: grabbing gateway host logs and edge-config diff. If we see patterns, we'll consider rolling a targeted fix.
sophia: for now: assign follow-up actions —
- liam: investigate gateway host networking/kernel parameters + escalate to infra if conntrack/pool exhausted
- alex: re-run canary of edge-config v2.14.1 in staging with increased load
- maya: collect prober logs, attach timeline and metrics to PD incident
- sophia: draft incident summary and send to #incidents postmortem channel after RCA
liam: will also add a temporary alert to watch for conn resets between gateway <> edge for 2h.
maya: attached logs and perf snapshots to INC-2026-00123: https://pd.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-00123/logs
sophia: great. marking mitigation complete in thread. PD: transitioning out of active paging but keeping incident open for RCA.
sophia: final note: runbook gap — prober fanout default (3) caused noisy pages for short-lived upstream blips. Recommend runbook update to default fanout=1 for production canaries or add suppression window for transient spikes.
liam: +1. I'll draft a CL for runbook updates and a config-change guard for edge deploys.
alex: thanks team. closing on-call handoff in 10m unless any regressions.
oncall-bridge: handoff complete. sophia remains incident owner for RCA. Incident status: monitoring -> post-incident review scheduled.
